intelligence.enrichment: The Celsius scale uses degree Celsius and °C, the Fahrenheit scale uses degree Fahrenheit and °F, and 37.0 °C is equivalent to 98.6 °F. A temperature value is interpreted correctly only when its scale and unit symbol are read together. The learner correctly applies this rule: The Celsius scale uses degree Celsius and °C, the Fahrenheit scale uses degree Fahrenheit and °F, and 37.0 °C is equivalent to 98.6 °F. The number is the temperature; °C, °F, and K are interchangeable labels.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 6 Science question. Chapter: Temperature and its measurement. The student must decide: Keep temperature scales, unit names, and symbols matched when reading or comparing temperatures. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE. If the stem numbers activities 1..n, every number must appear in an option (or in a structured part's first-class options). Two-tier (choose, then reason) is welcome: put A/B/C on part.options, not typed into part text.
